# Fleet V4 4.0.2 qualification and owning-lead handoff

Fleet V4 4.0.2 combines the existing V3 lifecycle, the one host byte authority, both delivered adapter families, the actual Pi registry/RPC worker driver, Grok native registration, and offline V3-to-V4 import. `fleet-v4-requirements.json` separates implementation, recording fixtures, model-free official runtime checks and actual-model evidence. The containing `release.json` pins the exact source commit and every package file hash.

Participating host tools and Pi read/edit operations use the existing authority. Native Claude/Codex/Grok file tools, Pi write/bash, shell, subprocesses, Git, formatters, other MCP and unmanaged writers retain their native paths and are outside mandatory byte mediation. Fleet does not implement universal enforcement, an OS sandbox or provider parity. Create is supported through the existing host write tool; native create/delete/rename are not universally mediated.

Scoped earlier Linux live evidence now includes Claude/Codex unattended workers, six independently checked websites and one 60-minute business task; token/cost accounting for that baseline remains incomplete. Grok passed three easy worker tasks and one direct-lead spawn of a real Claude worker on a later explicit package. Native Windows hub, security, executable identity, queue, scope and worker-lifecycle qualification used synthetic providers. These reports predate the final release archives and do not establish final-package provider parity. Pi real-model acceptance remains unknown. AGY is first-party internal use only and is not shipped, by owner decision. See [4.0.2 release notes](../RELEASE-NOTES-4.0.2.md) for exact commits, reports, measurements and limitations.

The Claude admission fix excludes only `seven_day_breakdown` metadata from utilization-window classification. Actual five-hour, weekly and model-specific windows still require finite utilization and available subscription allowance. Extra usage, custody, identity and no-credit gates remain. This fix alone does not prove native Claude account binding or successful live execution.

REQUIRED: preserve delivered history and frozen cohorts, use the single authority, retain native permissions and distinguish results from lead acceptance (owner requirements 1–8). CHOICE: merge exact delivered histories and add a final matrix rather than replace either adapter family. UNKNOWN: final independent source/package acceptance and successful remaining native model flows. Resolve these through the continuing verifier and owning client leads; registration or synthetic tests cannot supply missing live evidence.

The private source handoff includes affected terminal receipts, both deterministic archive builds, manifest verification and deliberate corruption/refusal results. Earlier failed attempts and pre-F1 checkpoint archives remain retained. The earlier baseline and 10k load measurement are reused, not repeated. No profile, account cache, credential, personal AGENTS or transcript is in the package; official Pi is an external native dependency.

Owner authorization already permits migration after qualification. The owning lead must apply `FLEET-V4-MIGRATION.md`: coordinate each root, quiesce through Fleet, preserve the previous runtime/source root, import to a separate private destination, inspect retained records, and explicitly activate/resume selected work. Frozen running cohorts cannot be moved underneath their runtime. Import starts zero workers. Rollback retains both roots and requires reconciliation of later effects; unknown mutations are never replayed. This integration worker has performed no installed cutover.

Codex custody keeps the required deployment pin: set `TELOGINS_CODEX_CUSTODY_CONFIG` to a readable absolute configuration path, and set `TELOGINS_CODEX_CUSTODY_HOST` to exactly that configuration's `host` field. Missing or mismatched pins refuse before SSH. Refusals now name the actual cause and repair: missing, unreadable or invalid configuration; missing accounts root; missing or mismatched host pin; failed or timed-out SSH; a service attestation refusal; or credit/spending policy refusal. The existing `FLEET_ACCOUNT_CUSTODY_UNAVAILABLE`, `FLEET_ACCOUNT_CUSTODY_INVALID`, `FLEET_ACCOUNT_HOME_INVALID` and `FLEET_ACCOUNT_SPEND_UNKNOWN` codes retain their roles, with a diagnostic `reason` on account-service errors. Service refusal messages include the stated reason with credential values redacted; process output and configuration values are never forwarded. Identity, single-holder custody, freshness, subscription and no-credit guards remain required at launch and thread admission.

See [custody diagnostics](FLEET-V4-SETUP.md#codex-custody-diagnostics) for individual causes and repairs.
